title: perf(canary): automated detection of latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: We run continuous performance canaries to detect latency and throughput regressions before rolling model or runtime changes to production. This PR implements an automated detection pipeline for canary signal regressions and couples it with rollout guards so unsafe canary results prevent traffic shifts. Motivation: recent incidents where KV-cache changes and batching adjustments caused small latency regressions that only surfaced after a gradual rollout. This creates a concrete, automated guardrail around canary metrics so human intervention is required for non-trivial degradations. Changes: - Add detector service that ingests canary metrics, computes baseline windows, and applies statistical tests (Welch t-test + effect-size threshold) to detect latency/throughput regressions. - Add hysteresis and sensitivity profiles to reduce flapping (fast, balanced, strict). - Integrate detector with rollout controller: on detection above thresholds the rollout controller cancels or pauses traffic shifts and annotates the rollout with failure reasons. - Add Prometheus metrics and tracing for detector decisions. - Add end-to-end e2e test harness and unit tests for detector logic. - Documentation updates explaining configuration and recommended thresholds. Checklist: - [x] Detector implementation + unit tests - [x] Rollout controller integration + integrational tests - [x] CI jobs updated and green - [x] Docs updated (docs/perf-canary.md) - [x] Rollout policy presets added (fast/balanced/strict) Notes: detection thresholds are configurable per-service and per-model. Default preset is "balanced" which we recommend for most hosted-api workloads. On canary runs we now compute 95% CI for latency percentiles and require both statistical significance and a minimum absolute regression to fire. We also check throughput regressions using bootstrapped median throughput comparisons. Related: ENG-2134, ENG-2201, SUP-4821.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice work. Two questions: 1) how do we avoid false positives for long-tail p95 spikes? 2) Can we expose a per-service sensitivity override in the console?

Asha Patel: Reply: We apply a dual-check: statistical significance + absolute minimum delta (configurable). The p95 smoothing window and minimum-delta are part of the sensitivity profile. We'll add an API surface for console overrides as a follow-up (ENG-2201).
Maya Singh: Request changes: tighten the default balanced profile to avoid unnecessary pauses for APIs with high variance. Also add more unit tests around edge cases (small sample sizes).
Asha Patel: Addressed: tightened balanced defaults, added bootstrap-sample-size guard and tests. PTAL.
Ethan Park: Approve after CI passes and docs link is clearer about recommended thresholds.
ci_summary: Initial run: lint failed on detector.go (fixed formatting) -> rerun. Unit tests initially had a flaky test (bootstrap edge case) which was stabilized by adding a minimum-sample check. Final status: all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e perf-canary job).
testing_notes: Added e2e test that runs a synthetic canary with injected latency perturbation and verifies detector triggers and rollout controller pauses. Added unit tests for Welch test edge cases and bootstrap throughput check.
notes_for_release_notes: Added automated canary regression detection and rollout guards; default 'balanced' sensitivity profile recommended. Teams can opt into 'strict' for low-latency workflows. See docs/perf-canary.md for configuration.
